subject: mathematics
question_text: If f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x², find (3f − 2g)(x).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.11, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 16(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards writing 3f(x) − 2g(x) with the substitution first and the simplified form with its domain second. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (3f − 2g)(x) — what the combination means, the simplified form, and the domain.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write what the combination means
steps.margin_note: First mark. A combination of functions is worked one x at a time: 3 times f(x), minus 2 times g(x), at the same x.
lines: f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x², both on R

accept: three f minus two g means three times f of x minus two times g of x
substitute so it is three into two x minus one minus two x squared
combine the two outputs at the same x
outputs ni combine cheyyali same x daggara
write three f of x minus two g of x first

steps.why: Functions are combined output by output: at each x you take 3f(x) and subtract 2g(x). Writing that line before substituting is what earns this mark.
steps.memory_tip: 3f − 2g acts at one x at a time: 3 times f(x), minus 2 times g(x).
common_mistakes: Multiplying the inputs, writing f(3x) − g(2x).

steps.label: Simplify and state the domain
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand and collect. Both parts are polynomials, so the combination is defined for every real x — write that down.
lines: f and g are defined for every real x,

recall.must_convey: That the simplified form is −2x² + 6x − 3 and the domain is R.
accept: six x minus three minus two x squared
the answer is minus two x squared plus six x minus three
both are polynomials so the domain is all real numbers
simplify and the domain is R

steps.why: The domain of a combination is the set where BOTH functions are defined. Two polynomials are defined everywhere, so the domain is R and no value has to be excluded.
steps.memory_tip: The domain of a combination is where both functions are defined. Two polynomials give R.
common_mistakes: Sign slip: writing 6x + 3 − 2x² after multiplying 3 into (2x − 1).
Leaving the answer without saying the domain is R.
